contracts.title: Actor Basic Attack uses beginBasicAttackFlow
contracts.summary: The stock actor-sheet BasicAttack control dispatches to LancerActor.beginBasicAttackFlow(), which constructs BasicAttackFlow and awaits flow.begin().

boundary.rule: Frame Conn may present and invoke the stock actor entrypoint, but native Lancer owns attack workflow construction, ordered steps, rolls, targeting semantics, chat output, and resulting native effects.

evidence.proof: The stock sheet switch maps BasicFlowType.BasicAttack to this.actor.beginBasicAttackFlow(...).
The actor entrypoint constructs BasicAttackFlow(this, ...) and returns await flow.begin().

contracts.title: BasicAttackFlow owns the stock basic-attack step order
contracts.summary: BasicAttackFlow defines the ordered stock attack workflow including target setup, attack HUD, attack rolls, self heat, and attack-card output.

boundary.rule: Do not reproduce or reorder BasicAttackFlow steps in Frame Conn. Invoke the native entrypoint and let native Lancer execute the registered workflow.

evidence.proof: The class declares the native ordered steps for a basic attack.

contracts.title: Actor Scan uses beginScanFlow with the selected target
contracts.summary: The stock actor sheet resolves game.user.targets.first() for Scan and passes it to LancerActor.beginScanFlow(target), which constructs ScanFlow and awaits flow.begin().

boundary.rule: Frame Conn may collect or prompt for a target, but native Lancer owns ScanFlow execution and scan semantics.

evidence.proof: The stock Scan branch obtains game.user.targets.first() and passes it to actor.beginScanFlow(target).
The actor entrypoint constructs ScanFlow(this, { target }) and awaits flow.begin().

contracts.title: Actor stat rolls use beginStatFlow(path, title)
contracts.summary: LancerActor.beginStatFlow(path, title) constructs StatRollFlow with the actor and supplied data path, then awaits flow.begin().

boundary.rule: Frame Conn may choose and present the stat path, but native Lancer owns StatRollFlow construction, modifiers, roll behavior, and output.

evidence.proof: The actor entrypoint constructs StatRollFlow(this, { path, title }) and awaits flow.begin().

contracts.title: Weapon items use beginWeaponAttackFlow
contracts.summary: LancerItem.beginWeaponAttackFlow() validates that the item is a weapon, constructs WeaponAttackFlow(this), and awaits flow.begin().

boundary.rule: Weapon attack execution should enter through the native item entrypoint rather than recreating weapon attack logic in Frame Conn.

evidence.proof: The native item method validates weapon type, creates WeaponAttackFlow(this), and begins it.

contracts.title: Item damage rolls use beginDamageFlow
contracts.summary: LancerItem.beginDamageFlow() validates weapon/NPC-feature type, constructs DamageRollFlow, and awaits flow.begin().

boundary.rule: Frame Conn should delegate eligible item damage-roll workflow construction and output to native DamageRollFlow.

evidence.proof: The native item method constructs DamageRollFlow(this, ...) and begins it after type validation.

contracts.title: Native damageCalc represents Resistance with multiple 0.5
contracts.summary: LancerActor.damageCalc accepts multiple values 0.5, 1, or 2; multiple === 0.5 is explicitly treated as resistAll. Native chat damage application resolves its target actor and delegates final application to actor.damageCalc(...).

boundary.rule: When Frame Conn needs native all-damage Resistance for an authoritative damage application, it should delegate through LancerActor.damageCalc with the native multiplier contract rather than reproducing armor/resistance/document-mutation logic.

evidence.proof: damageCalc validates multiple against [0.5, 1, 2] and defines resistAll as multiple === 0.5 before native armor/resistance processing.
The native chat damage control resolves the target LancerActor and delegates final application to actor.damageCalc with multiple/addBurn/AP/paracausal options.

contracts.title: Shutdown is a native Lancer status mutated through Actor.toggleStatusEffect
contracts.summary: Native Lancer defines shutdown as a first-class status identity and derived actor status, while embedded Status items apply their LID through Actor.toggleStatusEffect(..., { active: true }). Frame Conn therefore uses the corresponding native toggleStatusEffect pathway for authoritative shutdown removal.

boundary.rule: Frame Conn may own Boot Up legality and action semantics, but native Lancer/Foundry owns shutdown status identity and mutation. Read native status state and apply/remove shutdown through Actor.toggleStatusEffect rather than directly mutating derived system.statuses.shutdown or creating a Frame Conn shadow flag.

evidence.proof: The native Lancer status registry defines the first-class status id shutdown and its presentation asset.
The native actor initializes shutdown inside its derived system.statuses state alongside the other authoritative status identities.

When a native Status item is embedded in an actor, Lancer delegates status application to actor.toggleStatusEffect(this.lid, { active: true }), establishing toggleStatusEffect as the native status-mutation pathway.

contracts.title: Lock On is a native Lancer status consumed by native attack execution
contracts.summary: Native Lancer defines lockon as a first-class status identity and derived actor status. Native attack execution removes the lockon effect when its targeting data records Lock On consumption.

boundary.rule: Frame Conn may own Lock On target acquisition, Sensors legality, Quick Action semantics, and application of the native status. Native Lancer/Foundry owns lockon status identity and native attacks own later consumption/removal. Apply lockon through the native status pathway rather than writing system.statuses.lockon or creating a Frame Conn shadow flag.

evidence.proof: The native Lancer status registry defines the first-class status id lockon and its condition icon.
The native actor initializes lockon inside derived system.statuses alongside other authoritative status identities.
Embedded native Status items delegate application to Actor.toggleStatusEffect(this.lid, { active: true }).
When native attack targeting data records usedLockOn, native attack execution removes the target actor's lockon ActiveEffect.
